evidence: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. 'sender' is optional: build_integration only sets it when state has one (integration.py:376-377), and the webhook only adds it on some paths (webhook.py:204-206). installation.py:44 already checks `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`, which shows the codebase expects it to be missing sometimes. Case: an older Integration row without 'sender' whose OrganizationIntegration was removed reaches this line, raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the error() page. Fix: use integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login") and treat None as a mismatch.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:379-396 (test_installation_not_found) sends state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05. The pipeline signature is a fixed md5 of the view class paths (src/sentry/pipeline/base.py:132-133), and every other test uses 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 (lines 235, 242, 338, 445, 707, 737). So OAuthLoginView fails the state check (integration.py:412-413) and returns the generic 'Invalid installation request.' page. The test also never calls init_path to start a pipeline. The 404 path that raises 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' (integration.py:356), which the old test asserted, is never reached. The test passes for the wrong reason and no longer covers the 404 path.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:425-429 wraps safe_urlread(req).decode('utf-8') and dict(parse_qsl(body)) in `except Exception: payload = {}`. The catch is broad and swallows errors without logging, so real failures such as decode errors or network problems are silent. However, the code never expects a ValueError from parse_qsl (it catches Exception), so that part of the claim does not apply. The fallback is also fail-closed: an empty payload leads to error() at lines 431-432. Compare OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token (src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py:282-307), which catches specific exceptions (SSLError, ConnectionError) and logs them. Narrowing the exception and adding logging would help debugging, but there is no correctness or security bug.
